tools.name: 800.com
tools.entry_price_terms: per month on yearly billing ($23 month to month)
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-08-13, read on their own plans page with both billing tabs open) No free tier. On yearly billing: Startup $19/mo, Small Business $49/mo and Complete $99/mo; the same three month-to-month are $23, $59 and $119, badged SAVE 15%. Enterprise is quote-only. Startup covers 1,000 minutes, 1 number, 1 user and 1 extension. Small Business covers 3 numbers, 3 users and 3 extensions, with minutes listed as unlimited subject to the Fair Usage Policy. Complete covers 1,000 minutes, 5 numbers (local, toll-free or vanity), unlimited users and extensions, 1,000 transcribe minutes and 500 AI Agent minutes. Every plan carries a 30-day money-back guarantee. Listings that still name Personal, Unlimited or Pro plans are out of date.

tools.name: accessiBe
tools.entry_price_terms: Micro · per month for up to 5,000 monthly visits
tools.price_note: (2026-09-10, read on their own pricing page) Four tiers for accessWidget, priced per monthly website visits, with both a monthly and a yearly rate on every tier: Micro $59/month or $490/year up to 5,000 visits a month, Growth $179/month or $1,490/year up to 30,000, Scale $479/month or $3,990/year up to 100,000, and Enterprise on quote above that. Micro covers automated scans and fixes every 24 hours, an accessibility statement and report, and email plus live chat. Growth adds a dedicated case manager, Google Analytics integration, multi-account and team management, and a two-day response target. Scale adds one hour with an ADA attorney, a yearly round of manual testing and validation by their experts, and custom fixes. Enterprise adds 5 to 10 attorney hours, on-demand testing, SSO and a dedicated account manager. The page opens on the yearly toggle, so $490 is the first figure a visitor sees; switching it to 'Billed monthly' shows the monthly rates above. Paying yearly saves about 30% against twelve monthly payments, which is what the toggle's own SAVE 30% label claims. No free plan and no trial is listed.

flags.evidence: An overlay sits on top of a site and adjusts it in the browser.

tools.name: ActiveCampaign
tools.entry_price_terms: per month billed annually (1 user)
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-08-17 in the browser; the figures below are the 'starts at' prices on annual billing, before you pick a contact count) No free plan, trial only. There are four tiers. Starter is from $15/mo with 1 user, limited segmentation and 5 actions per automation. Plus is from $49/mo with 1 user, standard segmentation, unlimited automation actions and landing pages. Pro is from $79/mo with 3 users, advanced segmentation, predictive and conditional content and attribution tracking. Enterprise is from $145/mo with 5 users, premium segmentation, SSO, custom objects and a dedicated account team. Your email send allowance is a multiple of your contact count — 10x on Starter and Plus, 12x on Pro, 15x on Enterprise. The bill then scales with list size: the per-contact ladder only renders after you select a contact count, which is why we could not re-verify our earlier reading of about $189/mo for Plus at 10,000 contacts on this pass. CRM pipelines, SMS and extra users remain paid add-ons.

tools.name: AdCreative.ai
tools.entry_price_terms: a month for 10 credits and 1 brand
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-08-15, read on their own homepage pricing table) Credit-metered, where one credit is one downloaded creative, and there is no free plan — only a 7-day trial with 10 credits. Three families, each with several credit steps. Starter is 1 user throughout: $39 a month for 10 credits and 1 brand, $89 for 15 credits and 2 brands, $139 for 30 credits and $189 for 50. Professional is 10 users and 10 brands: $249 for 50 credits, $339 for 75 and $400 for 100. Ultimate is 20 users and 25 brands: $999 for 100 credits, $1,099 for 150 and $1,399 for 200. Credits expire at the end of each billing cycle and do not roll over.

tools.name: ADP
tools.price_note: (2026-08-15, read on their own site) ADP shows no public pricing for RUN anywhere on its site, and we checked four places before saying so. /pricing returns a 404, and so does /pricing.md. The RUN product page offers only a “Get Pricing” button. And the dedicated package-comparison page lists all four tiers with “Get pricing” under each one and not a single figure. The tiers are Essential Payroll, Enhanced Payroll (adds ZipRecruiter, State Unemployment Insurance and garnishment payments), Complete Payroll & HR Plus (adds basic HR support) and HR Pro Payroll & HR (enhanced HR support and staff perks). A promotion was running when we read it: three months of free payroll, marked “Ends 8/27”, with terms behind an asterisk.

flags.evidence: Ask for the per-employee-per-month rate and the per-payroll-run fee separately.

tools.name: Adwisely
tools.entry_price_terms: per month minimum on Self-Serve
tools.price_note: (price re-verified 2026-09-10) Read on adwisely.com/pricing; every figure below stood unchanged from our previous reading on 2 August 2026. Both plans charge 10% of the ad spend Adwisely manages, with a monthly minimum that acts as a floor rather than a fee on top: $49 on Self-Serve and $249 on Concierge (managed). At $5,000 of monthly spend the Self-Serve fee is therefore $500, not $549, and total monthly Adwisely fees are capped at $3,250 (re-read 15 September 2026). 7-day free trial, no setup fee.

tools.name: AfterSell
tools.entry_price_terms: a month at 200 monthly orders, capped at $999.99
tools.price_note: Three plans, each metered by monthly order volume, read on aftersell.com/pricing and on the Shopify App Store listing on 22 September 2026 (re-verified 22 September 2026). The entry prices are quoted at 200 monthly orders: Post-Purchase $34.99 a month, capped at $999.99; Pre-Purchase $59.99, capped at $599.99; Complete $79.99, capped at $1,359.99. Complete is the other two together, which the vendor prices at 15% under buying them separately. Go over a volume tier and the fee steps up to the matching one on its own, with that cap as the ceiling. Every plan carries a 30-day free trial, all charges are billed in USD, and the Free plan on the listing is for development and partner stores only. Checkout upsells are Shopify Plus only and now sit inside Post-Purchase and Complete rather than being billed separately. Rokt Thanks, the third-party offers on the confirmation page, is free with no minimum order volume and pays up to $0.80 per order; for stores above 1,000 monthly orders whose primary market is the US, Canada, Australia or the UK those earnings are credited against the subscription dollar for dollar. Aftersell Max, for high-volume stores, is custom-priced and publishes no figure. One number we could not account for: a $19.99 sits above the $79.99 on the Complete card, in the same white heading type and not struck through, and neither the page nor the FAQ explains it — the FAQ says Complete starts at $79.99. Check your own checkout total before you commit. This replaces the single order-volume ladder we recorded on 5 September 2026 ($34.99 for 0-500 orders, $54.99 for 501-1,000, $99.99 for 1,001-2,000); that ladder is on neither page any more.

flags.evidence: Three plans, each metered by monthly order volume, read on aftersell.com/pricing and on the Shopify App Store listing on 22 September 2026 (re-verified 22 September 2026).

tools.name: AgentNest
tools.entry_price_terms: Starter · per month for 100 successful automated fixes, billed in USD every 30…
tools.price_note: (read 2026-08-19 on apps.shopify.com/agentnest) Four tiers, and the split between them is unusual: the diagnosis is free and you pay only for the repairs. Free: unlimited catalogue scans, a catalogue readiness score, product-level issue reports and the full findings view. Starter $19 a month: 100 successful automated fixes a month, one-click fixes for all eligible issues, product-level recommendations. Growth $49 a month: 1,000 fixes a month, revenue-priority catalogue insights, fix history and progress tracking. Scale $99 a month: 5,000 fixes a month, advanced revenue-priority insights and bulk catalogue fixes. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days, and no tier shows a free trial. The billing unit is a 'successful automated fix', and the listing never defines it. Whether one fix is one product, one field on one product, or one alt text on one image is the difference between $19 covering a hundred products and a hundred images. It is also the only variable separating the three paid tiers. Developer Ecommerce Storez, 1255 23rd St NW, Washington DC; the app launched on 6 August 2026 and has no reviews at all.

tools.name: AhaSlides
tools.entry_price_terms: a month billed yearly (NL price - varies by country)
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-09-06) AhaSlides prices regionally, so the currency and the amount depend on where you buy from; the figures below are the reading from a Netherlands location on 6 September 2026, and your own country's page may show a different rate for the same tier. Free is 0 for up to 50 participants, with unlimited events and unlimited presentations but only 5 Quiz and 3 Unscored slides per deck. Essential is €7.25 per month billed yearly and lifts the ceiling to 100 participants, adding unlimited interactive slides, analytics and exports, and folder management. Pro AI is €10.65 per month billed yearly, raises the ceiling to 2,500 participants and adds the AI features, custom branding, Q&A moderation and priority support. Enterprise is quote-only, listed at up to 100,000 participants with SSO and SCIM offered on demand. Two discounts sit on top: yearly billing is advertised at up to 67% below monthly, and team licences bought together save up to a further 20%. AhaSlides' own USD listing puts Essential at $95.40 a year, which is the same tier at a different regional price rather than a second plan — so check the page from your own country before you budget.

flags.evidence: The advertised savings assume annual commitment, and the free tier's five-quiz-slide cap nudges real quiz use toward paid.

tools.name: Airia
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-09-10) Quote-only. Airia used to publish a ladder: a free tier, Individual around $50 a month and Team around $250. That page is gone — both airia.com/pricing and www.airia.com/pricing now redirect to airia.ai/docs/build/interface-options/usage_limits, a developer documentation page titled Usage Limits on a different domain, while airia.ai/pricing answers 200 with a shell that carries no text at all without JavaScript, and we found no amount anywhere on the site on 10 September 2026. Every deployment is therefore quoted after a sales conversation. Treat any $50 or $250 figure still in circulation, including in older versions of this review, as historical rather than current.

tools.name: Airwallex
tools.entry_price_terms: a month per active Spend user plus a team-size platform fee
tools.price_note: (2026-08-28, read off their own pricing page and fee table; no rate below has changed since 1 Aug 2026) FX conversion 0.5% above the interbank rate for major currencies and 1% for all others. Local transfers to 120+ countries free; SWIFT transfers $15–$25 each. Payment acceptance 2.8% + $0.30 on domestic cards and 4.30% + $0.30 on international cards; local payment methods $0.30 plus method-specific fees. Corporate cards carry no international fees and up to 2% cash rebate on local USD spend. Account plans: Explore free, Grow $12 per active Spend user/month plus a platform fee that varies with team size, Accelerate custom. Their table adds limits the earlier reading did not record: the first 10 Spend users are free and the $12 rate runs to 250 Spend users; the monthly fee is charged per business legal entity, with up to 3 entities included and $1,000 per additional entity; subscription and usage-based billing cost 0.50% per successful transaction while invoicing is free; and USD balances earn a Yield rate that Airwallex restamps daily rather than fixing per plan — on 5 September 2026 the page showed 3.22% on Explore, 3.37% on Grow and 3.49% on Accelerate, and its own footnote reads that the indicative rate is the 7-day annualised historical rate of the underlying funds as of 4 September 2026, net of fees. Read those three figures as a moving number carrying the date the page gave it, not as a plan feature: they were 3.21%, 3.36% and 3.48% when we first recorded them on 28 August 2026. (yield re-verified 5 Sep 2026) Platform API and embedded finance are quote-only. Two gaps we had left open got a partial answer on 17 September 2026, when Airwallex pointed us at its fee schedule. Dispute handling does carry a price, but only the Canadian entity publishes it: airwallex.com/en-ca/terms/fee-schedule prints 15 CAD per chargeback request and 0.30 CAD per refund request, both excluding whatever the card network passes on. The US pricing page lists dispute management as a feature with no fee beside it, so treat the Canadian figures as the shape of the charge rather than as your rate. The Grow platform fee is still not a number anywhere: both the US pricing page and the Canadian schedule say only that it is based on the total number of Spend users, so ask for it before you budget. Re-verified 2026-09-19 on airwallex.com/en-us/pricing: every published rate above is unchanged — FX, transfers, acquiring, the 0.50% on subscription billing, the free first 10 Spend users, the 250-user ceiling on the $12 rate and the $1,000 per entity beyond three. The yield figures still read 3.22%, 3.37% and 3.49%, but their footnote now dates the seven-day annualised rate to 18 September 2026 instead of 4 September. That is the clearest evidence yet that these three numbers are a daily restamp rather than a plan feature: same values, new date. The Grow platform fee is still not printed anywhere.

tools.name: AISDR
tools.entry_price_terms: a month (or $2,400 a year), 1 user
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-09-09 on AiSDR's own pricing page) There are three published plans. Solo is $250/mo or $2,400/yr for a sales team of one: 200 AI-researched contacts a month, 1 user, 1 domain, 3 mailboxes, month-to-month. Explore is $900/mo or $8,640/yr (800 contacts a month, unlimited users, 2 domains, 6 mailboxes), and Scale $2,500/mo or $24,000/yr. Annual billing takes 20% off. Explore and Scale carry a quarterly commitment; Solo runs month to month. Managed service is extra: +$149 per campaign, or fully managed from +$2,500/mo. Enterprise is custom. Priced by contact volume rather than by seat above Solo.

tools.name: Algomo
tools.entry_price_terms: a month (no per-seat pricing)
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-09-14 on newmode.ai/pricing and the homepage) Plans start at $200 a month with no per-seat pricing - and that single sentence is still the entire public price list, unchanged since our July and August readings. The pricing page carries exactly two plans, Growth and Enterprise, and both buttons say 'Let's chat' and 'Book call': no amount, no contact slider, no self-serve tier. Growth lists 1:1 personalized LinkedIn ads, AI-generated ad copy, website personalization, CRM integration and email support; Enterprise adds unlimited campaigns, custom integrations, a dedicated success manager, priority support and advanced analytics. tools.name: AltText.ai
tools.entry_price_terms: per month (100 credits/mo)
tools.price_note: (re-verified 26 Aug 2026) Credit-metered — one credit = one image. Free trial: 25 credits, no credit card required. Monthly: Bronze $5/mo (100 credits/mo, 5¢ per image), Silver $19/mo (500), Gold $59/mo (2,000), Titanium $119/mo (5,000), Platinum $229/mo (10,000). Annual buys the same yearly credit volume at a discount the page labels 17-31% off: $49/yr (1,200 credits), $189/yr (6,000), $489/yr (24,000), $1,179/yr (60,000), $2,199/yr (120,000). One-time credit packs are 50 credits for $3 with no subscription; beyond 120,000 credits a year is custom enterprise pricing. Unused plan credits roll over when the plan renews on its normal cycle, and banked rollover credits and one-time packs stay in the account — but the FAQ states that changing plans, up or down, forfeits the current period’s unused plan credits. You can cancel anytime and keep what is unused, and every feature ships on every plan. Two multipliers change the real per-image cost: advanced formats (AVIF, HEIC, HEIF, JP2, SVG, TIFF) bill 2 credits and are paid-plans-only, and each additional translation language costs 1 more credit per image.

tools.entry_price_terms: per month for 15,000 (Booster $799 for 50,000)
tools.price_note: (re-verified 13 September 2026 on bitscale.ai/pricing, extended on 11 September 2026 from inside a free account; every headline figure unchanged since 1 September 2026) The meter is credits. Free is $0 with 200 credits, no card required, capped at 20 action columns per grid and 50,000 rows. Growth is $349 a month for 15,000 credits, 30 action columns and 100,000 rows, with a two-way HubSpot integration and inbound integrations like RB2B, Factors and Vector. Booster is $799 for 50,000 credits and 50 action columns, adding curated scraping scripts, a private Slack channel and Salesforce integration. Enterprise is quote-only but publishes a floor most vendors hide: annual billing at $15,000 and above, adding SOC 2 and SSO, priority support, role-based team access and Snowflake pipelines. Annual billing takes 10% off. Two lines in the plan table change the arithmetic and are easy to miss. Credits roll over up to three times the plan allowance on Growth and Booster, and not at all on Free, so a quiet month is banked rather than lost. And a credit is spent only when a data provider returns a valid result -- the pricing FAQ says failed lookups, formula columns and CRM syncs are always free -- so a waterfall that finds nothing costs nothing. The page also contradicts itself twice: the comparison table gives all four tiers 100+ data sources while the Free card says 10+ B2B data sources, and the Growth and Booster cards both promise Unlimited Actions while the same page's table caps action columns per grid at 30 and 50. The step from Free to Growth is still the one to plan for: 200 credits to 15,000 with nothing in between, so the bill goes from nothing to $4,188 a year in one move. Monthly company and people search is metered separately at 2,000 on Free, 15,000 on Growth and 50,000 on Booster. Two things the pricing page does not tell you, both read on 11 September 2026. First, what a credit actually buys: Bitscale's own credit documentation prices a found email or phone number at one to twelve platform credits per successful result, depending on how many providers the waterfall is allowed to try, with an AI enrichment at one to two credits a run and a BitAgent website scrape at one. Calls that come in through the API cost nothing. Second, the free tier runs two meters rather than one, and the account screen shows both: 200 platform credits for enrichment and a separate 2,000 search credits for Find People and Find Companies, each resetting monthly. The upgrade panel inside the product also carries a Growth benefit the plan cards leave out -- three hours a quarter with a GTM engineer -- and states plainly what Free locks: credit rollover, more than 20 action columns per grid, the 100+ providers and the inbound integrations.

The monthly-billing prices ARE readable now, which they were not on 19 August 2026: the page carries both figures as data attributes on each amount and swaps them with script, giving Hobby $29, Starter $69 and Team $199 a month when billed monthly. Against the annual rates that is a 34% saving on Hobby and about 30% on Starter, Team and Business & Scale, so the “Save 30%” chip understates the entry tier. Unlimited AI outputs, re-generations, media clipping, audiograms, AI image generation, custom prompts, community prompts and 2000+ word outputs are on all three published tiers, as are 60+ transcription languages, unlimited file uploads, a 10GB maximum file size, 50 maximum concurrent uploads, the Media Library, and the Zoom, Google Drive, Zapier, RSS and YouTube/TikTok/Instagram imports. tools.name: CloudTask
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-08-19, read on their own pricing page) Two hiring models, both published, plus one deposit. A one-time $299 deposit starts your search — asked “Do you charge a monthly platform fee?” their FAQ answers “No. There is a one-time $299 deposit to start your search. That is the only fee outside the models above.” — and the deposit applies toward your buyout or your first placement. Direct Hire costs 20% to 30% of first-year base salary, paid once and quoted per role, with a 6-month replacement guarantee (one replacement, same job description) and US W2 employment available. Managed Staffing is billed as one all-in monthly rate per person covering salary, compliance, payroll and support — that rate is not published, and it is the number that decides what this costs. Graduating a managed hire onto your own payroll is possible after six months for a one-time placement fee quoted at that moment; no amount is published. tools.name: Datarails
tools.price_note:
(read 2026-08-25 on www.datarails.com/pricing) There is no public price. Datarails publishes three plans — Professional, Premium and Expert — and every one of them carries a Request Quote button where the number would be. The page frames that as a feature: “Get a custom quote tailored to your needs. Complete cost transparency, with no consultant fees—ever.”

What the page does publish is the shape of the ladder, and it is unusually explicit about what changes between tiers. The comparison table lists the same feature set on all three plans: reporting, planning, dashboards, Data Mapper, Lookups, Workflows, Submit Button, File Boxes, Filters, version control, the Datarails AI Suite, the FinanceOS AI Connector and permissions. Only two rows differ. Professional gives 1 integration and 2 users with standard support. Premium, marked most popular, gives 2 integrations and 5 users with premium support, and adds AI Storyboards, described as board decks in one click. Expert gives 3 integrations and 15 users with premium support, plus one “additional product included” — the line beyond FP&A runs to Datarails Month-End Close, Datarails Cash, Datarails Spend Control and Datarails Desk, and the page does not say which of those the extra slot may be spent on.

So the meter is seats and connected systems, not features. The page states no currency, no billing period, no minimum term and does not say whether a quote is annual, and there is no free plan, no free trial and no self-serve signup: the only entry point on every page of the site is Request Demo or Request Quote. Treat any Datarails figure you have seen quoted elsewhere as unverified — on 25 August 2026 the vendor's own pricing page contains no amount at all.

One of those unpublished terms the vendor will answer if you ask. On 31 August 2026, through its partner team, Datarails told us that customers typically commit to an annual term, that billing can run monthly across that year, that users can be added as a team grows, and that adding modules or capabilities beyond the core platform can carry an extra cost that depends on the scope of the expansion. That is the vendor's own account rather than a published rate, so it belongs in your quote in writing — but it does answer the term question the pricing page leaves open.

tools.entry_price_terms: per month plus $0.75 per ticket, 7-day trial
tools.price_note: (re-verified 8 September 2026 on apps.shopify.com/event-tickets; every figure unchanged since 1 September 2026) Four tiers, and every one of them charges twice: a monthly fee and a fee per ticket processed. Lite is free to install and takes $1.00 per ticket. Growth is $19 a month and $0.75. Standard, the tier the store marks Popular, is $49 and $0.50. Professional is $189 and $0.25. The paid tiers carry a 7-day free trial. Read that structure the right way round: the monthly fee is not what you are buying, it is what you pay to lower the per-ticket rate, so the correct plan follows from your ticket volume and nothing else. The crossings are exact. Lite and Growth cost the same at 76 tickets a month; below that Lite wins. Growth and Standard cross at 120. Standard and Professional cross at 560. So a store selling 300 tickets a month pays $199 on Standard against $244 on Growth and $264 on Professional -- the middle tier, and the store's own Popular label happens to be right for that range. One feature line changes that arithmetic and sits above the crossover: Collect fees on every ticket sold appears on Standard and Professional only, so passing the per-ticket cost to attendees is itself a paid feature. Beyond that, feature differences barely enter into it until Professional, which is where reserved seating, Klaviyo and Mailchimp integrations, the multi-vendor dashboard and priority support live. The app is published by Staytuned and carries a 4.4 rating from 320 reviews.

The toggle reads 'Annual plan, paid in full' and 'Annual plan, billed monthly' - both are twelve-month plans, and no month-to-month option exists on the page. Paying by the month therefore costs $131.88 a year on Editor ($1.89 more) and $167.88 on Editor+ ($7.89 more) without shortening the commitment. A perpetual licence, Foxit PDF Editor 14, is $209.99 once per user for Windows or macOS, covering editing, conversion, OCR, forms, security and fill-and-sign but not the web app, the AI Assistant, Smart Redact, the document management system or any cloud feature; Foxit's own FAQ argues the subscription is better value because it unlocks AI, cloud integrations, unlimited cloud storage, the full DMS and eSign integration, and notes that Adobe no longer sells perpetual Acrobat licences to new customers. An education discount is applied automatically at checkout when you register with a school email address; Foxit does not publish the rate. tools.name: Geotargetly
tools.entry_price_terms: Dev · per month billed yearly ($12 monthly)
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-09-20 on their own pricing page, from a European exit) 14-day free trial, no card. Six tiers: Dev $12/mo, Startup $24, Growth $49, Business $99, High Traffic $199, Enterprise from $349 — billed yearly $9, $19, $39, $79, $159 and from $279. The digits are unchanged since 31 August. CURRENCY: Geotargetly prices the same digits in more than one currency, so the symbol you see depends on where you are. Reading the page from Europe on 19 September returned these figures with a dollar sign; reading it from the same exit on 20 September returned the identical figures with a euro sign — €12, €24, €49, €99, €199 and from €349 monthly, €9 to €279 billed yearly. The numbers did not move, only the symbol did. We quote the dollar list here because that is the currency the rest of this page's figures were read in, but a European buyer should expect to be billed the same number in euros, which is not the same amount of money — do not convert one into the other. IMPORTANT: on 19 September the page was running a live 50/50 price split test on visitors from 32 countries (US, UK, CA, AU, NZ and 27 EU states), assigned by a 30-day cookie; the alternative set is about 20% higher — $14, $29, $59, $119, $239 and from $419. The amounts above are the lower, control set, which is also what visitors outside those 32 countries see; a fresh session on 20 September landed in that same control set. The page's own price table additionally enumerates an eight-step Enterprise ladder the plan card does not show: $349, $429, $519, $599, $699, $869, $1,299 and $1,739 monthly, $279 to $1,391 as yearly monthly-equivalents, with annual totals $3,350 to $16,694. Standard annual totals are $108, $230, $470, $950 and $1,910 — two dollars above twelve times the advertised monthly-equivalent on all but Dev. That table did not render on the 20 September reading, which served only the six plan cards, so those ladder and annual-total figures still carry their 19 September date. All plans include country, state and city-level targeting on unlimited domains. The meter is PAGEVIEWS, not visitors: a pageview is consumed for every page visit, and separately for each product in use; Geo Links consumes one on link click only. No refunds, and quota does not roll over to the next billing cycle. On quota exhaustion you get 2 days to upgrade or re-subscribe before services stop, with email alerts at 30%, 10%, 5% and 0%. Per-tier pageview quotas are still NOT reliably readable: the page shows one quota figure (500,000 monthly, 6,000,000 yearly) for the whole ladder at once, which cannot be right for six tiers.

flags.evidence: The meter is PAGEVIEWS, not visitors: a pageview is consumed for every page visit, and separately for each product in use; Geo Links consumes one on link click only.

tools.price_note: (Classic re-verified 2026-09-03 in a live browser session on both tabs and both billing toggles, unchanged since 2026-08-04; the GlideOS plans were re-read the same day after a restructure) The classic spreadsheet-to-app builder still has a genuinely free tier: unlimited drafts, one editor, up to 25k rows. Its paid plans are unchanged, but they now live on glideapps.com/classic/pricing instead of the main pricing page. On the individual tab, Explorer starts at $19 per month billed yearly or $25 billed monthly (one app, 100 personal users, 250 updates, up to 25k rows) and Maker at $49 per month billed yearly or $60 monthly. On the business tab, Business starts at $199 per month billed yearly or $249 monthly, with unlimited apps, 30 users included, 5,000 updates and up to 100k rows. Extra users are $5 each on annual billing and $6 on monthly, and extra updates cost 2 cents each. Enterprise is quote-only. VAT is added at checkout, and Business comes with a 14-day free trial. Glide now sells two products from two pages. What glideapps.com/pricing shows today is GlideOS, the newer AI builder, on its own separate subscription, and its plan ladder was rebuilt between our August and September readings. The Free, Solo and Team tiers we recorded on 4 August 2026 are gone; as read on 3 September 2026 the ladder is Free, Basic at $25 per month, Plus at $50, Pro at $125 and a quote-only Enterprise. Free carries 2 team members, 10 projects and limited credits, with no published apps. Basic adds 100 credits, 2 published apps and 1 enabled workflow. Plus gives 250 credits, 3 team members, 5 published apps, 20 projects and 5 workflows, with credit bundles up to 10,000 a month. Pro starts at 5 team members with 500 credits, 50 credits included per member, unlimited published apps and workflows, premium integrations and the option to build with your own agent over MCP. Two things that used to be on the page are not any more: the $10 per additional member above five, and Glide's note that annual GlideOS plans were coming. So the GlideOS prices are still monthly only, and what a sixth seat costs is no longer published. Credit top-ups are capped at one a month on Basic and two on Plus, and are unlimited on Pro and Enterprise. One caveat on the row ceilings, from Glide's own partner team on 18 August 2026. The 25k limit applies to synced spreadsheet sources regardless of plan type, and the 100k+ figures apply to their Big Table data source. So which ceiling you hit is set by where the data lives as much as by what you pay. They also confirmed the Individual and Business tabs on the pricing page are audience segmentation rather than two halves of one plan ladder.

Starter is €9 a month billed yearly, or €11 month to month, for 3 profiles, 1 user and 30 posts a month. Launch is €33 billed yearly (€39 monthly) for 5 profiles, 1 user and 100 posts. Custom starts at €116 billed yearly and covers 5 to unlimited profiles and 1 to unlimited users, with white-label reporting, API access and a dedicated CSM. The ladder has changed since our 26 August reading over a US connection, which listed Launch $39, Scale $79 and an Excel tier at $139: Excel no longer appears as a named plan, its price and its white-label, API and CSM features now sit under Custom, and Starter is new below Launch. The profile count is the dial that moves the price, so a quote taken at five says little about what a team managing thirty will pay — and the tiers differ in users, posts and history, not just in profile allowance.

tools.name: IDrive
tools.entry_price_terms: a month for 100 GB
tools.price_note: (2026, re-verified 24 Sep 2026) Free 10 GB Basic tier. IDrive Mini is $0.25/month for 100 GB ($0.83/month for 500 GB). IDrive Personal is $9.99/month for 5 TB, shown discounted to $6.99/month with annual billing (save 30%), scaling up to $99.99/month ($69.99 discounted) at 100 TB. Those are the yearly-billing figures the page opens on; switch it to the Monthly tab and the same Personal 5 TB plan is $11.99/month, and a two-year plan is advertised at up to 50% off the first year: Personal 5 TB is $179.82 for two years against a standard $239.76, which is exactly half off year one plus a full-price year two. Business on the Monthly tab starts at 1.25 TB for $59.99, not at 500 GB. Team starts at the same $9.99/month ($6.99 discounted) for 5 computers and 5 users on 5 TB; Business starts at $19.99/month ($13.99 discounted) for 500 GB with unlimited users. Add-ons: server backup $5/month/server on Mini, Personal and Team (Business includes servers), and Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace backup at $20/seat/year. The honest catch is on the pricing page in IDrive's own words: the discounted price applies to the first year of the selected plan, and standard pricing applies from the second year onward. Two further conditions sit in the same footnotes: going over your storage limit costs $0.25/GB/month on Personal and $0.50/GB/month on Team and Business, and the discount is for new signups only and is not available if you sign up from IDrive's mobile apps. IDrive Express bulk shipment: one free backup a year on Personal, three a year on Team and Business, then $59.95 per request. Every figure above read the same on 24 September 2026 as on 4 September and 27 August 2026.

There are two plans and the cheaper one is almost certainly not for you: the Development plan is free, unlocks every feature, and the listing states its limit plainly — development and partner stores only, with billing activated on upgrade. Monthly Plan is $2.99 a month, or $28.70 a year with the annual saving the listing puts at 20%, and it carries the falling effect, the AI logo maker, custom image upload, appearance and density controls, the marquee logo slider, dozens of holiday presets, support for all themes and live chat support. tools.name: Influencer Hero
tools.entry_price_terms: a month, or $454 a month billed annually (also $519 billed quarterly)
tools.price_note:
(pricing matrix read 18 September 2026 in documentation the vendor sent us; the public ladder at influencer-hero.com/pricing was read the same week and shows the quarterly column) Four plans, and the figure you see depends entirely on the billing term you pick. Billed monthly: Standard $649, Pro $1,049, Business $2,490. Billed quarterly: $519, $839 and $1,992 — and this is the column the public pricing page leads with, which is why $519 is the number most people quote. Billed annually: $454, $734 and $1,743. The advertised 20% and 30% savings check out exactly against the monthly rate ($649 × 0.8 = $519.20, × 0.7 = $454.30), so the discounts are real and the headline is simply the discounted one.

What each plan carries: Standard is one seat, 1,000 reach-outs a month and 20 influencer payouts. Pro is three seats, 5,000 reach-outs and 200 payouts. Business is eight seats, 10,000 reach-outs and 500 payouts, and Enterprise has unlimited payouts. On 19 September the Business plan card still said unlimited while the comparison grid on the same page said 500; Influencer Hero told us the card was a leftover from a site revamp, and when we re-read the page on 24 September 2026 the card and the grid both said 500 for Business and unlimited for Enterprise. Enterprise is custom on every other axis. Every plan carries a three-month minimum term and there is no free trial, so the smallest real commitment is three months of Standard: $1,947 billed monthly, or $1,557 if you take the quarterly rate. The influencer CRM, the outreach automation and the UGC tracking are in every plan; the ladder is gated on quota and seats. Influencer payouts can run through bank direct debit (ACH in the US, Bacs in the UK, SEPA in the EU) with only Stripe's processing fee passed through: 0.1% to 0.4% by the vendor's own account, around 0.4% to 0.5% effective by its Payout Manager post, with US ACH capped at $5 a payout, against the 2-3% that card processors typically charge.

tools.name: Livestorm
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-09-05 on their own pricing page) There is still no plan price. Pro is sold as attendee credits, bought as a yearly pack up front, with sessions up to 4 hours and unlimited team members; Enterprise is quote-only with sessions up to 12 hours. The rate depends on the currency you pick on the page, and the two are not conversions of each other: €2.50 per attendee in euros, $3.00 in dollars. Their own definition, worth reading twice because it decides your bill: one credit is spent for each unique participant, per session, over a 12-month period. Someone attending two different sessions costs 2 credits; the same person joining live and later watching the replay of that session counts once. Registrants who never show up cost nothing, and your own team members never consume credits. tools.name: Mycroft
tools.price_note: (read 4 September 2026 on www.mycroft.io/pricing) Mycroft has no public pricing: three packages, and not one number between them. Platform is the entry tier and the only one whose button says Get started rather than something sales-shaped; it bundles the full GRC platform for SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, HIPAA and more, a Cloud Native Application Protection Platform, security, AI and privacy awareness training, 24/7/365 threat intelligence and monitoring, a Trust Center, and what Mycroft calls basic Agentic AI workflows. Scale says Book a demo and adds penetration testing, continuous third-party risk management, a customer success manager and expanded AI workflows. Managed says Talk to sales and adds customised frameworks, customised AI workflows and a dedicated CISO who doubles as your success manager. What the page never does is price any of it: no monthly figure, no per-seat rate, no starting-from, no annual floor, not even for the tier you are invited to start by yourself. We looked past the pricing page before writing that down, because the claim is usually wrong. The FAQ page, the product pages, the CMMC-as-a-Service page and the machine-readable llms.txt all describe the packages in detail and none of them names an amount; the sitemap holds no second pricing page; and the raw HTML of /pricing carries no hidden figure either. So the tiers tell you exactly what you get and leave what you pay entirely to a call.

tools.name: Ownr
tools.price_note:
(prices read 22 September 2026 in a live browser on www.ownr.co/pricing, all amounts in Canadian dollars - Ownr sells into Canada only) The page has two selectors, jurisdiction and structure, and shows different cards for each combination, so there is no single ladder. It also now leads with the discounted price rather than the regular one, which is the first thing to correct for.

Sole proprietorship, Ontario: the card reads Free with an RBC bank account, plus applicable taxes, under a banner offering to save CA$49 on the regular price by opening one. So the published regular price is CA$49 and the advertised price is nothing. It covers the government fees, business name searches, the registration number and documents, document storage, chat support and Ownr Perks.

Incorporation is priced identically in Ontario and federally: the Online Minute Book Plan at CA$199 with an RBC bank account, renewing annually at CA$199, and the Managed Corporation Plan at CA$698 with an RBC bank account, renewing annually at CA$599. Both cards state they include the one-time government and filing fees. The banner offers CA$300 off for opening an RBC account, which puts the regular first-year price at CA$499 and CA$998.

British Columbia, which the selector labels Canadian Provincial, costs more to enter and the same to keep: Online Minute Book CA$399 with an RBC bank account renewing at CA$199, Managed Corporation CA$898 renewing at CA$599, with the same CA$300 rebate - so CA$699 and CA$1,198 at the regular price. The renewal rate is the same in every jurisdiction; only the incorporation year differs.

Three add-ons exist and all three are locked to the Managed Corporation Plan: Managed Shareholders at CA$297 a year including three shareholders and CA$99 a year for each one after that; Managed Employees and Contractors at CA$99 a year including three and CA$39 for each extra; and an Employee Stock Option Plan at CA$999 a year.

Two things on that page do not agree. Every plan card says it includes the one-time government and filing fees, while the small print under the comparison table says prices do not include government registry fees and that such fees are payable at the time of filing. Read the quote at checkout rather than the card.

And the RBC offer is not a cashback that arrives later. Ownr's help centre describes it as an instant discount taken at payment - CA$49 off a sole proprietorship, CA$300 off an incorporation - on the condition that you open an RBC business bank account at a branch within 60 days. Miss that window and the rebated amount is charged back to the card you paid with; open the account later and it is refunded once you tell Ownr's team. If a branch visit inside two months is not certain, budget the regular price.

tools.name: Parallel AI
tools.entry_price_terms: per month for 2,000 or $297/mo for 9,000
tools.price_note: (read on 11 September 2026 on parallellabs.app/pricing, which stamps itself 'Last updated: 2026-08-18') The meter is credits, and there are two separate pools. Plan credits come with the subscription: Pay As You Go is $0 with 50 credits and no card, Entrepreneur $99 a month for 2,000 credits and 2 companies, Business $297 for 9,000 credits and 10 companies, and Enterprise is quote-only with SSO, on-premise deployment and dedicated support. Data credits are a different pool, bought once and never expiring, and they are the only part of the product priced per action: 1 data credit per lead or contact returned, 2 per matched enrichment lookup through the API or an agent, and a lookup that finds nothing is free. They run $25 for 500 down to $175 for 5,000, so between 5.0 and 3.5 cents a lead. The two pools expire differently, and the page says so in two places that sit far apart: plan credits 'reset on the 1st of each month', while purchased credit packs and data credits never expire. What the page never says is how many PLATFORM credits an action costs. Content generation, an agent conversation and an outreach step are all simply 'credits' with no published rate, so the 2,000 on Entrepreneur is a quantity without a unit until you have run your own work through it. Per credit the tiers differ by a third: 5.0 cents on Entrepreneur against 3.3 on Business, which is three times the price for four and a half times the credits. Running out has a tier-shaped answer -- the FAQ offers extra credit packages on the Business plan and the Pay-As-You-Go card offers top-ups, but Entrepreneur sits between them with no stated top-up route, so the $99 tier's answer to an empty meter appears to be the $297 one. Seats do not add capacity: every seat in a company shares one monthly pool, and extra seats are $15 a month ($12 annual). The add-ons are where the bill can outgrow the plan -- an extra company is $20 a month ($16 annual), an extra white-label instance $50, and anonymous website pixel identification runs $75, $250 or $500 a month for 500, 2,000 or 5,000 resolutions. On the free tier the limits are real: a 200k context window against 1M on every paid plan, 30 days of chat history instead of unlimited, no App Builder, and model access listed as 'Limited' with response times 'limited on bandwidth and availability'.

tools.name: Parim
tools.entry_price_terms: a month (published floor)
tools.price_note: (re-read 2026-09-17 on parim.co/pricing; unchanged since 20 August 2026) One number is published and the rest is not. The page says pricing starts from £47 per month with unlimited users on every plan, but each of the three tiers — Starter, Pro, Premium — carries a ‘Request Pricing’ button rather than a figure. Their own explanation: they price on the functionality you need and the number of shifts you schedule each month. So the £47 is a starting point, not a plan price. What the tiers contain is published even though the prices are not. Starter is scheduling: employee scheduling, a configurable shift list, locations and roles, time off requests, automated shift reminders, separate staff and management apps, shift creation from the app, and SIA badge expiry reminders. Pro adds time and attendance: scheduling patterns, configurable timesheet and people lists, a pay run report, configurable automated pay schedules and CSV exports. Premium adds shift cancellation tracking, timesheet analytics, payroll export, staff management by employment type, an invoicing report, a position coverage report, pay lock and client shift requests. Five modules sit outside the three tiers with no price attached — events manager, checkpoints (NFC and iBeacon), incident reporting, check calls and asset tracking. The quote form asks for a number of employees, not a number of shifts.

flags.evidence: Unlimited users sounds like the generous part, and it is — until you notice what replaces per-seat pricing: a bill that scales with shifts scheduled.

tools.name: PartnerStack
tools.price_note: (read 2026-08-26 on partnerstack.com/pricing) There is no public price at any tier. PartnerStack publishes three plans — Launch, Growth and Enterprise — and every one of them carries a Book your demo button where the number would be; /plans is a 404. What the page does publish is what moves between tiers, and it is unusually specific. Launch gives you affiliate link tracking OR lead and deal registration — you pick one — plus marketplace access, partner payments built for B2B sales cycles, onboarding and enablement tooling, CRM integrations and their AI and MCP connector. Growth adds deeper integration support, a learning-management solution, partner challenges and incentives, MDF management and payments, and segmentation by performance or strategy. Enterprise is the only tier with full access to link tracking AND both registration motions at once, and adds custom workflows, a designated CSM with semi-annual business reviews, partner introductions and priority support. So the meter is not seats or volume as far as the page will say — it is which partner motions you are allowed to run, and the choice between tracking and registration on the entry tier is the line worth reading twice.

tools.name: Payoneer
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-09-14 on payoneer.com/about/pricing/, the canonical fee page their own llms.txt names; the page itself carries "Last updated on 1 January 2026") Free to open; the cost is in the fees. Receiving into a receiving account in your local currency is free, in a currency that is not your local currency 1% (minimum $1). Receiving by credit card or PayPal up to 3.99% + $0.49; by US ACH bank debit or an EU or UK bank account 1%. Withdrawing to a bank account in your own country and currency $1.50 flat; to a bank account in another country or currency 1.2%-4%, even when no conversion happens, and in some countries a minimum fee of up to $20 may apply. Moving funds between your own Payoneer balances 0.50%. Annual account fee $29.95, charged only if less than $6,000 arrives in any 12 consecutive months and not charged in the first year on paid annual plans. Certain US customers, depending on registration date, instead pay a flat $1.50 per withdrawal or payment up to $50,000 a month and up to 0.5% above that. Businesses moving over $50K a month are pointed at a custom package. Workforce Management is a separate product line with its own price list, read on payoneer.com/workforce-management/ on 5 September 2026: Employer of Record from $199 per employee a month (110+ countries), Agent of Record from $99 per contractor a month (160+ countries), and the Contractor Management System from $19 per contractor a month, all three 'starts at' figures behind a demo and marked 'pricing may vary by country, services and engagement type'. Our partner link on this page belongs to that Workforce Management programme, so it lands on the workforce partners page rather than on the free payments account.

tools.name: PDWare
tools.price_note: Quote-only, re-confirmed 25 September 2026: pdware.com has no pricing page (/pricing returns 404) and every route ends in a 'Request pricing' form or a guided demo, with no amount anywhere on the homepage. What the site does publish, in a Pricing & licensing section on its FAQ page that carries no numbers, is the shape of the quote: licensing is based on the size of the planning group and on the types of users on the system, and packages exist for workgroups of 50 users, 100 users, and enterprise-level deployments, with multi-team and enterprise licensing handled by an account executive at sales@pdware.com. There is no self-serve trial, but there is a pilot: the FAQ says many organisations start with one, validating the software on their own data before committing to a long-term subscription. The same picture holds off-site — the ResourceFirst Workgroup Package is listed on Microsoft's commercial marketplace by Portfolio Decisionware Inc. with no price at all and a contact-me action, its offer identifier carrying the band 10-50.

tools.name: Pecan AI
tools.price_note: (read 2026-08-27 on pecan.ai/pricing) No public price at any tier. Pecan publishes three plans — Starter, Team and Business — and each one carries a Talk to sales button where the number would be, with a fourth enterprise route for special deployment and granular explainability. Billing is annual only and Pecan states there is no setup fee. What the page does publish is the meter, and it is not the one most buyers expect: the tier is set by monthly prediction batches and stored rows, not by seats. Starter gives 2 batches a month and 500M rows, Team 10 batches and 2Bn rows, Business custom batches and 5Bn rows; support runs from in-app only, to in-app plus Essential enablement, to Pro enablement. A batch is one run against a dataset, so two a month is a fortnightly cadence — the number that decides your tier before any conversation about team size.

Credits buy access to a single pool of models — images on Nano Banana, Nano Banana 2, Nano Banana Pro and GPT Image 2; video on Seedance 2.0, Seedance 2.0 Fast, Seedance Pro, Kling 2.5, Kling V3, Veo 3 Fast, Veo 3 Quality and Wan 2.5 — and the pricing page publishes a full table of how many generations each plan buys on each model, which is where the real prices are. One caution before you buy: the page quotes Pro monthly twice and not at the same figure. The plan card says $49 a month; the comparison table directly beneath it heads the same column $29 a month, for the same 1,100 credits. Both were on screen together on 16 September 2026.

tools.name: Piktochart
tools.entry_price_terms: per member per month billed yearly ($15 monthly)
tools.price_note: (re-verified 6 September and again 19 September 2026 on piktochart.com/pricing/, US dollar view; the 19 September reading came from a VPS-uitgang because the Mac’s TLS stack is too old for the site; the plan amounts are unchanged from our 6 August 2026 reading) Free is $0, Pro is $15 per member per month billed monthly or $10 billed annually ($120 a year), Business is $20 monthly or $17 billed annually ($204 a year), and Enterprise is quote-only from 101 members. Free stops at 2 PNG downloads — a flat total, not two a month — 1 GB of storage, 60 AI credits and free templates only, and is capped at four members (one owner plus three). Pro adds unlimited PNG downloads, premium templates and icons, 500 AI credits and 100 GB, and the annual rate is what the page calls 33% off. Business, 15% off annually, adds PDF and PowerPoint export on top of PNG, the Brand Kit (unlimited brand colours, fonts and logos), 1,000 AI credits and 250 GB. Enterprise adds SSO/SAML, workspace management, a dedicated account manager and a one-off hour of training. Three further cards on the same page price other audiences, and two of them beat Pro on both price and capability. Education is $39.99 per member billed annually — the card splits the cents into a separate element, which is why a careless reading gives $39; the FAQ prints the full figure — with 250 AI credits, a limited Brand Kit and unlimited PNG, PDF and PowerPoint downloads, and requires a valid educational email address. Campus is quote-only above 3,000 seats. Nonprofit is $60 per member billed annually with the same 250 credits, limited Brand Kit and unlimited PNG, PDF and PPT downloads. The page's own FAQ calls those two 'a 76% discount' and 'a 64% discount' from its annual pricing, which works back to a list of about $167 a year — a figure that appears nowhere on the page, where annual Pro is $120 and monthly Pro annualises to $180. The page can be switched between USD, GBP, EUR, SGD, MXN and INR. No free trial is offered on the paid tiers — the free plan is the trial — and you can cancel anytime, though the FAQ adds that refunds are generally not given under the Terms of Use and are reviewed case by case, and that purchases of $168 or more can be settled by bank deposit.

tools.name: Pingtree
tools.price_note: (2026-08-27, read on their own pricing page) Self Service is “From $199” per month with a free trial included, and Managed Services carries a starting cost of $2,500, “scoped with your account team”. That is a rebuilt price list: the six named tiers that were on this page in July are gone, and there are now two paths rather than six. Self Service is the whole platform driven by Pingtree Copilot, with core usage — leads, pings, clicks and storage — included each month, overage billed after month close, unlimited users on role-based access, and validations and throughput added as volume climbs. Managed Services is a scoped engagement priced on volume, markets and complexity: implementation, integrations and workflow design are included, along with a dedicated Solutions Engineer, ongoing account optimisation, priority support with SLAs where required, and optional retainers for media, creative and ad ops. There is also an “Explore Pingtree Free” entry straight into the app. No overage rate is published on the page, and the trial no longer carries a stated length — in July it said 14 days.

We could not get the monthly column to render from the US on three attempts, so this is the annual view only — by Pipedrive's own 42% figure, paying month to month costs meaningfully more. The trial is 14 days with no credit card, though the affiliate landing page our own link leads to advertised 30 days, with LeadBooster, Smart Docs and Projects included, when we followed it on 3 September 2026. LeadBooster, Projects, Campaigns, Web Visitors and Smart Docs are optional paid add-ons on top, from €13.33 for Campaigns up to €41 for Web Visitors — and those add-ons are where a Pipedrive bill usually stops matching the number you picked off this page.

tools.name: Poptin
tools.entry_price_terms: per month billed annually ($25 monthly), 10,000 visitors
tools.price_note:
(read 18 September 2026 in a live browser on poptin.com/pricing, in both product modes and both billing cycles, with the in-app billing page at app.popt.in checked alongside it) The page opens with a question — “What are you looking for?” — and the answer changes the whole ladder.

Pick Poptins, the popup product, and every tier carries a figure. Free is $0 forever with 1,000 unique visitors a month, one domain and unlimited poptins. Basic is $20 a month billed annually ($240 a year) or $25 billed monthly, for 10,000 visitors and one domain. Pro, marked Most Popular, is $47 annually ($564) or $59 monthly, for 50,000 visitors and four domains. Agency is $95 annually ($1,140) or $119 monthly, starting at 150,000 visitors with a dropdown that climbs through 300,000, 500,000, 750,000, one million and two million, plus unlimited domains and premium support. The stated 20% annual saving checks out at all three rungs: $60 off $300, $144 off $708 and $288 off $1,428.

Pick Emails & Poptins, the combined product, and the ladder loses its prices. Free is $0 for 250 active contacts, 500 emails and 1,000 visitors. Growth — the tier the page marks RECOMMENDED — shows the word “/month” and no amount at all, at any of the eighteen contact bands in the selector. Enterprise is quote-only in both modes.

The meter is unique monthly visitors, and their FAQ defines it: anyone who loads a page carrying the snippet in the last 30 days, counted once however many sessions or pages they open — unless they clear cookies or switch device or browser, in which case they count again.

tools.name: Post Purchase Upsell Hero
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-09-19 on apps.shopify.com/post-purchase-upsell-hero and the vendor's own site; amounts unchanged since 31 August, USD) One plan, Performance, free to install, at $0 a month plus usage charges. The usage table, read from the listing's own pricing-estimator data, has two tiers: 2.5% on the first $20,000 of upsell revenue in a month, and $0 from $20,001 up. In practice that is a commission with a ceiling — the app cannot charge more than $500 in a month, and a month in which it sells nothing costs nothing. There is no paid tier above it: unlimited funnels and offers, one-click upsell and downsell, AI product recommendations, analytics and A/B testing and market translations all sit on that single plan. Charges are billed in USD every 30 days. The vendor's own site publishes no prices at all — its pricing link leads to the same single-plan listing — so the listing is the only place the meter is stated. Neither page defined how 'upsell revenue' is measured, so we asked, and the vendor answered in writing on 21 September 2026 with permission to quote it. The figure is net: the amount the customer is actually charged for the accepted upsell item, after any discount set on that offer, and nothing from the original cart is included. Refunds and cancellations of an accepted upsell are reversed automatically through Shopify — proportionally for partial refunds, with the 2.5% coming off alongside, and no support ticket needed — while refunds of original cart items never move the figure, because they were never billed. There is no multi-day attribution window either: the offer exists only on the Shopify post-purchase page between payment and the order confirmation, and the merchant sets how long that moment stays open, with a default of 20 minutes, any value from 1 to 59 minutes, or Shopify's own 60-minute default. The vendor says the full rule now sits in its help center under Pricing and billing. That is the vendor's account of its own meter, dated and on the record, but it is not something we have audited against a live bill.

flags.evidence: meter: percentage · upsell revenue generated by the app
On discounted or thin-margin add-ons the same percentage is a far bigger share of the profit, and the meter reads revenue either way.

tools.name: PreOrder Now
tools.entry_price_terms: a month (tier keyed to Shopify plan size)
tools.price_note: (re-verified 13 September 2026 on zenpire.tech/app-listing/pre-order-now/, every amount unchanged since 10 September; the amounts come from Zenpire's own page because the app is not installable from the Shopify App Store: apps.shopify.com/preorder-now, checked 14 September 2026, carries it as "PreOrder Now WOD" by Website on Demand Studio, LLC and states the app is currently not available there, and a store search for Zenpire returns no apps) Five tiers, and they are named after your Shopify plan rather than after what the app does. Free is $0 and covers your first pre-order product, with mixed-cart warnings and email tech support. Then Shopify Basic is $19.95 a month, Shopify Standard $39.95, Shopify Advanced $59.95 and Shopify Plus $99.95 -- all with unlimited pre-order products. Read the feature lists side by side and the point becomes obvious: Basic and Standard list exactly the same five features (unlimited pre-order products, collection page badges, preorder discount, pre-order by product tag, Quickview support), and Advanced and Plus list exactly the same three (unlimited pre-order products, "ALL FEATURES of Basic Shopify & Shopify plans", dedicated success manager support). So the ladder is not buying you capability; it is charging you according to the size of store Shopify says you run. A Plus merchant pays five times what a Basic merchant pays for the same badges, the same discounts and the same tagging. The one real step is Advanced, which adds a dedicated success manager. Note that partial payments, which the FAQ advertises as a feature, are named on none of the five plan cards, so the tier that carries them is unstated. All charges are in USD and recur every 30 days.

flags.evidence: Free is $0 and covers your first pre-order product, with mixed-cart warnings and email tech support.

tools.name: ProtectMyOrder
tools.price_note: (re-read 2026-09-18) The App Store route has closed. apps.shopify.com/protectmyorder, the page this review was built on, now returns “This app is not currently available on the Shopify App Store. If you have support questions, contact ProtectMyOrder directly.” — no plan block, no review record, no install button. With it goes the only plan that carried a figure you could read before signing up: 19.99% of delivery protection revenue with a minimum charge of $20 per month, billed in USD. ProtectMyOrder's own pricing page, re-read the same day, is unchanged and still sells three tiers, all priced as a share of upsell revenue rather than a monthly fee. Standard at 19.99% adds a profitability guarantee, a gradual roll-out to 50% of visitors, fully customisable design and wording, and an assigned support agent. Carbon at 24.99% adds automatic carbon calculation and offsetting for every delivery, with a choice of project. Pro at 44.99% puts their own agents on your shipping-claim support with 24/7 cover and ten-minute replies, and for a further 30% of upsell revenue they assume the liability for refunds and replacements as well — 74.99% in total. Volume discounts are by call for brands above $20m of online revenue. Getting in is now described as a request rather than an install: add the app, fill in an installation request form, accept a collaborator-access request, and their team does the rest; merchants not on Shopify are pointed at email, live chat and an API. No monthly minimum appears anywhere on that page, and the site's own footer still links “Download Shopify app” to the listing that no longer resolves.

tools.price_note:
(read 19 September 2026 in a live browser on repete.me/pricing and on the App Store listing at apps.shopify.com/reorder-service) There is no subscription and no tier. rePete is free to install and takes a percentage of the sales it claims to have caused, billed in USD, on three rates that are defined by a clock rather than by judgement.

Direct Sales is 3%, charged when rePete nudges a customer to reorder a product and they complete the purchase within 24 hours. Assisted Sales is 1%, charged on the same nudge when the purchase lands within 7 days. Upsells and cross-sells are 5%, charged on any extra items the customer adds beyond the reorder product itself.

What the page rules out is as useful as what it charges: no SMS fees, no email fees, no per-contact fees, no push fees, no app fees and no minimums. So the messaging channels — email, SMS, WhatsApp and on-site — carry no cost of their own, which is unusual in a category where SMS is normally metered separately. There is no published ceiling, no volume discount and no negotiated rate: the percentages are the whole price list. The app is built by Bold of Winnipeg, Shopify's first front-end app developer and the team behind Bold Subscriptions; it launched on 4 July 2025 and holds 5.0 from nine reviews.

All four list the same six feature groups: Amazon & Walmart, AI repricing technology, min & max calculation, analytics, connectivity and integrations. The four tiers are set out above; what the page does not tell you is what each step actually buys. Accelerator doubles your revenue ceiling and leaves the SKU count alone, and Standard does the reverse — fifteen times the catalogue with the ceiling removed — while the seller ID and user counts never move at all. So the middle tier is for turnover and the top tier is for range, and a shop that needs neither is paying for the other one. The revenue ceilings themselves are printed without any period attached; Seller Snap told us in writing on 24 Jul 2026 that both are calculated per month, so read them as $15,000 and $30,000 a month. Annual billing saves a flat $900 a year on both Accelerator and Standard — the same money, but 30 percent off the smaller plan against 15 percent off the larger one. Every tier carries a 15-day trial with no credit card, and in the monthly view each price is labelled 'Starting at'. Seller Snap confirmed to us in writing on 24 Jul 2026 that readers coming through our link get 10% off for their first three months; it runs through the link, there is no code to enter. Update: asked directly, Seller Snap confirmed by email on 24 July 2026 that the Starter and Accelerator revenue caps are calculated per month. Their pricing page still does not say so — we are passing on the vendor's answer, not something you can verify on the page yourself. One thing on the page has changed and it is not a price: a banner above the plans offers 'your first month for only $1 when you subscribe before 2026', a deadline that had already passed when we read it on 26 Aug 2026, so treat it as decoration rather than an offer until support confirms it.

tools.name: TextExpander
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-08-18 on the vendor's own pricing page; USD per user/month billed annually, excluding tax) The line-up was rebuilt since our July reading and it now starts at free. Free is $0 forever with no credit card, Pro $5 (billed annually at $60), Business $10 (billed annually at $120), Enterprise quoted. Annual billing is sold as two months free against paying monthly; the page does not print the monthly amounts next to the plans, so we do not quote them. The free plan is real but deliberately narrow: 5 active snippets out of an unlimited library, one snippet swap every two weeks, 3 teams, 5 team members and no snippet activity history at all. That history — what lets you see changes and restore deleted snippets — is 24 hours on Pro, 7 days on Business and unlimited only on Enterprise. Team members stay capped at 5 on Free and Pro; unlimited members start on Business, which is also the first tier with single sign-on (Google SSO on Business, all providers plus SCIM on Enterprise). A 30-day trial with full access to every feature and no credit card sits alongside the free plan. The page still carries an important pricing note for international customers, which we could not open on this reading, so treat the listed USD amounts as pre-tax.

tools.name: TheTop
tools.price_note:
(read 19 September 2026) TheTop publishes no price. The navigation carries no pricing link, every button is Book a demo, and the page this review's figures came from is gone: thetop.com/pricing returns a hard 404, as do /pricing/ and /plans.

The $8 a month and $80 a year this review used to quote were withdrawn along with the product they belonged to, and cannot be bought today. Until September this was a personal assistant on a single tier, built around a morning brief from Gmail and a calendar. TheTop is now enterprise software sold through a sales call.

Read the figures on their site carefully, because it is full of dollar amounts that are not prices: the dashboard mock-ups show an AI invoice of $196,090, a month billed at $137,644 against a $176,920 baseline, and $39,276 saved. Those illustrate what the product reports, not what it costs. Nothing on the public site says what you would pay for TheTop itself.

What the site does commit to about commercial shape: deployment is single-tenant, one dedicated instance per customer; onboarding runs in three steps that start read-only (connect analytics, watch for about a month to establish your number, then point traffic at the Engine); and no traffic migration is needed on day one. Expect a contract quoted against your own AI spend rather than a list price — ask for the pricing basis in writing before the demo, because a layer that bills against measured savings and one that bills a flat platform fee are very different deals.

On Plus that unquoted rate is the whole variable, because the 300 is only the entry fee.

tools.name: TnC
tools.entry_price_terms: Basic Plan · per month on the App Store listing, or $47.94 a year, for the checkbox…
tools.price_note:
(read 2026-08-25 and re-verified 2026-09-09 on apps.shopify.com/terms-and-conditions-checkbox, listed as “TnC: Terms and Conditions Box”, and in the vendor's own pricing article at www.effectify.help) The monthly ladder is $7.99, $12.99 and $14.99, and it has held there since the August rise: read on 24 August 2026 the same three plans, carrying the same feature lists, cost $6.99, $9.99 and $12.99. What moved between 25 August and 9 September is the annual price. It used to be $67.12, $109.12 and $125.92, roughly a 30% saving; the listing now shows $47.94, $77.94 and $89.94 and says “save 50%”. That is exactly six months' money for a year at every tier, where in August it was seven-tenths of the year, so the annual route got cheaper while the monthly one did not move at all.

Four plans on the listing, and the free one is not for you. Development Stores is free and carries every Pro feature, but the listing states it is for development and partner stores only and that payment will be activated on upgrade — so the “Free plan available” line at the top of the listing describes a partner sandbox rather than a free tier for a store that takes orders. Basic is $7.99 a month or $47.94 a year and covers the AI terms-and-conditions checkbox with support for Buy It Now and express checkout buttons. Advanced is $12.99 a month or $77.94 a year and adds the consent date logged into the order's details plus the ability to show the checkbox for specific countries and products. Pro is $14.99 a month or $89.94 a year and adds newsletter and contact forms, translation of the checkbox into multiple languages, the checkbox in Shopify POS and an AI-powered policies generator. Every paid tier carries a 7-day free trial, and the listing states charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days.

The vendor's own pricing article, re-read on 9 September 2026, has not followed. It still prints the old annual rates of $67.12, $109.12 and $125.92, still puts the annual saving at approximately 30%, and still answers its own question “are there any hidden fees?” with “No. All pricing is transparent and listed above” — while the App Store listing, which is where the charge is actually raised, prints a different number for the same plan. It is also the only page where a fifth plan appears at all: a Plus Plan at $19.99 a month or $167.92 a year, for Shopify Plus merchants only, adding “the ability to show the checkbox in the actual Checkout page of your store”. The Plus Plan is the one monthly rate that has never moved, so the gap between the top listed plan and the hidden one is $5. The article also notes that uninstalling during an ongoing billing period still incurs that period's charge.

Developer Effective Apps, trading as Effectify, at 13 Max Nordau, Ashdod, Israel; the app launched on 2 December 2019, carries Shopify's Built for Shopify badge, and stood at 550 listing reviews with a 4.9 average on 9 September 2026, up from 514 two weeks earlier.

tools.name: Trackr
tools.entry_price_terms: per month or $96/yr (400 shipments/mo)
tools.price_note: (price read 2026-09-12) Four tiers and no free plan, billed in USD every 30 days through Shopify: Basic $10 a month or $96 a year for 400 shipments a month, Standard $45 or $432 for 2,000, Advanced $150 or $1,440 for 9,000 and Enterprise $250 or $2,400 for 18,000. Annual billing saves 20% and every tier carries a 14-day trial. The feature list is identical on all four — branded tracking page, estimated delivery dates, email, WhatsApp and US-only SMS updates, Apple and Google Wallet tracking, Klaviyo, Omnisend, Segment and chatbot integrations, product upsell and translation — so the only thing the ladder sells is shipment volume. The Shopify listing does not say what happens past your allowance. The vendor's own page does: parceltrackr.com/pricing, read the same day, prints $0.05 per extra shipment on every tier. That number decides whether you upgrade or overrun, because in-plan a shipment costs 2.5 cents on Basic, 2.25 on Standard, 1.7 on Advanced and 1.4 on Enterprise — so an overrun is priced at two to four times what the same shipment costs inside the plan. The two sources also disagree about the trial: the listing offers 3,000 and 5,000 bonus trackings on Advanced and Enterprise, the vendor page 1,500 and 2,000.

Pricing is quote-only. An earlier version of this entry carried monthly figures attributed to unnamed third-party sources; those are not on the vendor's page and could not be traced to a named source, so they have been removed rather than repeated.

There is also no self-serve way to try it. The FAQ question “Can I try Trainual before committing to a subscription?” is answered with an invitation to book a demo, not with a trial, so a sales conversation is the only route in. Two things are quantified beyond the fee: the implementation team aims to have interviews completed and content in the account within 10 business days, and 500+ templates are included, with 400+ expert-built courses sold separately as a premium courses add-on whose price the page does not give.

tools.price_note: (re-read 2026-09-18 on apps.shopify.com/zendrop and on zendrop.com/pricing — the two do not carry the same ladder) On the Shopify listing: free to install, with three paid tiers, Beginner $29, Pro $49 and Plus $79 a month. What separates them is not features but how many products you may link to your store. The free tier allows none at all (“No linked products allowed”), Beginner covers 1-20, Pro 21-100 and Plus 101 or more; the feature list on all three paid tiers is identical (trending products, Zendrop Academy, Zendrop AI access, custom branding). Product and shipping cost is charged per order on top of every plan, and the listing states that external charges may be billed by Zendrop separately from your Shopify invoice. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Rating 4.6 from 1,258 App Store reviews, up from 4.5 from 1,191 on 19 August 2026; the spread is 83% five-star (1.0K), 7% four-star (92), 2% three-star (19), 1% two-star (15) and 7% one-star (84). The listing does not carry Shopify's “Built for Shopify” badge. Developer Zendrop, 5499 North Federal Highway, Suite R, Boca Raton, FL, 33487, US; the app launched 4 November 2020. On zendrop.com/pricing the ladder is different: Free $0, Pro $49 a month or $399 a year, and Plus $79 a month or $549 a year, marked Most Popular. There is no $29 Beginner tier on their own site, and the annual rates appear only there — $399 is $33.25 a month and $549 is $45.75. The Summer Promo recorded here on 19 August 2026 (65% off annual Plus for the first year, advertised as a $357 saving, plus $100 in order credits, ending 31 August 2026) is gone: the page carries no percentage-off offer at all on 18 September 2026. Their own site also lists products the App Store listing does not mention, including AI-Built Stores, an AI Ad Generator and an MCP Server for connecting AI agents to a store.

tools.name: ZoomInfo
tools.price_note: Sales-gated, and re-verified as such on 2026-08-17: no public rates, no monthly billing and no free plan, with the pricing URL refusing plain requests and neither of our monthly captures retrieving a figure. Contracts typically start around $15k and the median runs near $32k a year, climbing once seats, credits and add-ons (intent data, international coverage) stack up — but those are third-party figures, not ZoomInfo's, and every deal is negotiated annually. Expect a multi-year push and price the credits, not just the seats.
